title: rucc corpus report, version 1
description: The machine readable summary of one corpus run. Written to reports/report.json. The schema version is in the report itself, in the schema field, and it is a string rather than a number so that a version can be a date if it ever needs to be. A field is added without a version bump. A field is removed or changes meaning only with one.

schema.description: The version of this schema the report was written against.

milestone.description: Which milestone of the compiler plan the corpus is written for.

tool.description: What wrote the report, with its version.

corpus_digest.description: SHA-256 over every case in the corpus. Two reports with different digests are about different programs, and comparing their numbers directly is a mistake. This is what rucc-corpus diff checks before it says anything.

cases.description: How many programs are in the corpus.

reference.description: The id of the toolchain the others are measured against.

levels.description: The optimization levels that were built.

totals.description: One entry per toolchain, counting every build it did across every level.

targets.description: The falsifiable claims the compiler plan makes, and whether this run met them.

size_model.description: One entry per toolchain, saying what -Os did to that toolchain's own output. Empty when the run did not build -Os, which is what the per-commit job does.

findings.description: Every result that was not what the generator said it would be. Empty is the good case.

measured.description: How much of this report was measured in this run. A result whose inputs all hashed to what they hashed before is read out of the record cache rather than built again, which keeps the verdict and keeps a timing that was taken on an earlier day. A tool comparing two reports for a timing regression should look here first.

results.description: How many case, toolchain and level results the run produced.

built.description: How many of them were compiled and run in this sitting.

reused.description: How many of them came out of the cache. Zero after a run with --refresh or --no-cache.

id.description: What it is called in every other part of this report. Chosen by whoever ran it, so that a report from a laptop and a report from CI line up even though the binary was in a different place.

version.description: The first line it printed for --version.

reference.description: Whether the others are measured against it.

tally.description: How a set of builds came out. Every build lands in exactly one of the seven verdicts, so pass through crashed sum to ran and skipped is the rest.

pass.description: Did what the generator said it would.

wrong.description: Compiled, ran, printed something else. The worst kind.

rejected.description: Refused a program that is valid C.

unimplemented.description: Refused a program that is valid C, having said itself that the construct is not built yet. Counted and reported, and not a failure.

accepted.description: Accepted a program that is not valid C, or rejected it for the wrong reason.

crashed.description: Fell over, timed out, or died on a signal.

skipped.description: Not built, because the case asked to be left out.

failures.description: Everything that is a bug, so wrong plus rejected plus accepted plus crashed. Not unimplemented, which is a gap the compiler declared, and not skipped.

pass_rate.description: Passes over ran, or zero when nothing ran.

compared.description: How many cases had a number on both sides, so the ratios below are medians over this many.

size_ratio.description: Median of this toolchain's executable section bytes over the reference's, at -O2. One is level with the reference and more than one is bigger.

text_bytes.description: This toolchain's executable section bytes summed over the facet at -O2, across exactly the cases size_ratio was taken over. Divide the sum of these by the sum of reference_text_bytes to get the code-quality target, which counts bytes rather than facets so that adding a facet cannot move it.

reference_text_bytes.description: The reference's executable section bytes over the same cases, per text_bytes.

speed_ratio.description: Median of this toolchain's run time over the reference's. Less than one is faster. Read speed_is_real before quoting it.

speed_spread.description: How far the repetitions of one program spread on this machine, as a fraction of the fastest, taken as the median over the same cases speed_ratio was taken over and over the wider of the two toolchains on each case. Nought would mean the machine held perfectly still. Null when the records kept no samples, which is every report written before they were kept.

speed_is_real.description: Whether speed_ratio is further from one than speed_spread is from nought. False means the difference between the two toolchains is smaller than the difference this machine produces running the same program twice, so there is nothing in it. The reports print the words inside the noise rather than the number when this is false.

instruction_ratio.description: Median of how many instructions this toolchain's programs ran over how many the reference's ran, at -O2. The same question speed_ratio asks, answered by a counter rather than a clock, so it reproduces to within a thousandth on a machine where the wall clock moves by a factor of four. Where this has a number in it, it is the number to read. Null on any machine that would not count, which is anything without perf and anything that will not hand a counter to an unprivileged process.

instruction_delta.description: How many more instructions this toolchain's programs ran than the reference's, summed over the same cases instruction_ratio was taken over, at -O2. Negative is this toolchain running fewer. This is the one to read and instruction_ratio is not, because a program in this corpus retires about a hundred and forty thousand instructions and about a hundred and eight thousand of those are the process starting up before main. That startup is the same code on both sides, so a ratio carries all of it in its denominator and comes out at one however the toolchains differed, and a difference carries none of it. Worth nothing when counted is nought.

counted.description: How many cases had an instruction count on both sides. Its own count, like memory_compared, because a missing instruction ratio says something about the machine the run happened on and nothing about the compiler.

compile_ratio.description: Median of this toolchain's compile time over the reference's. Less than one is faster to compile.

memory_ratio.description: Median of the largest high water mark in this toolchain's process tree over the reference's, while building. Null on any platform where the harness cannot read a process tree, which is everything that is not Linux.

disk_ratio.description: Median of this toolchain's whole executable file size over the reference's. Not the same measurement as size_ratio, which is the code alone. This one includes the runtime, the symbol table and the linker's padding, so it is what a build costs on disk rather than what the optimizer decided.

data_ratio.description: Median of this toolchain's initialized data in the image over the reference's. Moves the opposite way from size_ratio when a compiler trades code for a table.

memory_compared.description: How many cases had a memory figure on both sides. Its own count rather than sharing compared, because memory is the one number here that can be missing for a reason that has nothing to do with the compiler.

ratio.description: A median ratio against the reference, or null when neither side produced a number. Never one as a stand-in for missing, because a missing measurement and a measurement that came out level are different facts. Medians rather than means throughout, because the corpus is full of tiny programs where one instruction is twenty percent.

target.description: One claim from the compiler plan, checked.

threshold.description: The number the claim has to beat.

source.description: How much C something is, counted once per case however many toolchains and levels the case was built with. This is the denominator for every cost in the report. A tool comparing two runs needs it to tell a compile time that moved because the compiler changed from one that moved because the corpus grew, and it is here rather than derived because nothing else in the file can answer that.

lines.description: Lines of C, with a last line that has no newline after it still counted as a line.

facet.description: One named transformation, and how every toolchain did on the programs written for it.

describes.description: What the facet is about, in one sentence.

reference_said.description: What the reference compiler reported through -fopt-info on these programs. Reference data and not a pass or fail signal. A high missed count means the transformation was available and the reference did not take it, which is a hint about the program rather than about anybody's compiler.

size_model.description: What -Os did to one toolchain's own output. Every other ratio in this report is one compiler against the reference at the same level. This one is a compiler against itself at two levels, which is a different question and the only way to ask it, because -Os is a different cost function rather than a cheaper -O2. A toolchain whose -Os output is the same size as its -O2 output has accepted the flag and ignored it.

compared.description: How many cases produced a size at both -Os and -O2 for this toolchain.

unmoved.description: How many of those came out at exactly the same number of bytes.

ignoring.description: Whether this toolchain is taking the flag and doing nothing with it. Every compared case came out the same size and the reference did move some of them. Not the same as unmoved equalling compared on its own: whole facets have no size against speed tradeoff in them, and on a run filtered down to one of those every toolchain comes out unmoved and none of them has done anything wrong.

against_o2.description: Median of this toolchain's executable section bytes at -Os over its own at -O2. Less than one is smaller code.

by_facet.description: The same ratio per facet, smallest first, so the facets -Os saves the most on come at the top.

finding.description: One build that did not come out as the generator said it would.

case.description: The case id, which is also the file name under programs.

summary.description: The finding in one line, for a list.

expected.description: What it should have printed, or the diagnostic it should have produced.

actual.description: What it printed, or what the compiler said.
